newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Conglomerate keeps Mauritius index rise in check.
newsitem.headline: Conglomerate keeps Mauritius index rise in check.

text.p: The Semdex market index at Stock Exchange of Mauritius (SEM) edged up by 0.63 points to 328.68 on Wednesday with a share price slump of conglomerate Ireland Blyth limiting its rise, dealers said.
Volume transacted totalled 6.13 million rupees on 293,319 shares from 4.86 million rupees on 283,486 shares on Monday.

Dealers said the market on the whole was continuing its climbing trend but this was not reflected by the Semdex marginal rise on Wednesday as gains were offset by Ireland Blyth which was down 80 cents to 13.30 rupees with 1,570 shares traded.
Ireland Blyth's share price fall on Wednesday was a shade below six percent, the maximum margin within which stocks are allowed to move at the SEM during any trading session.
Analysts said amid a correction from the stock market's year low in late October, the conglomerate's share price rally during the past few weeks was too rapid to be sustainable.
"Ireland Blyth rose from 11.50 rupees on October 18 to 14.10 rupees last Monday. This represents a massive gain of nearly 25 percent in four weeks," said an analyst from a fund management concern.

In August, Ireland Blyth reported a 40 percent slump in its interim profit for the six months ended 30 June 1996 to 25.4 million rupees as compared to the corresponding 1995 period, on turnover of 1.50 billion rupees.
Most other stocks rose or remained stable on Wednesday and the market correction from its depressed levels during the past couple of weeks was seen losing steam.
Mauritius Commercial Bank was unchanged at 73 rupees on 17,746 shares and State Bank of Mauritius remained at 8.70 rupees on 113,619 shares.
Conglomerate Rogers climbed one rupee to 90.50 on 2,020 shares and oil company Shell (Mauritius) added 40 cents to 13.90 rupees on 2,325 shares.
